posts.title: TRAFFIC ALERT: Here’s why Myers Way offramp from southbound Highway 509 is closed
posts.description: (Also posted on partner site West Seattle Blog ) Jim Edwards sent us that photo of state troopers arriving at an area he described as “showing signs of a washout under the left side of the (southbound Highway 509 offramp to Myers Way), visible from the Cloverdale interchange.” Shortly after he texted us, WSDOT announced the ramp was closed until further notice because of “an incident.” We followed up with WSDOT and they’ve confirmed the “incident” is what Jim saw: “The ramp is closed pending further onsite assessment by maintenance and geotechnical engineers. At this time it appears that there is a washout – the extent of which is TBD,” WSDOT spokesperson Elizabeth Mount tells us. ADDED: Here’s a photo tweeted by WSP:

posts.title: Day 1 of White Center Library Guild’s Holiday Bazaar and Book Sale
posts.description: (Also published on partner site West Seattle Blog ) It’s a big weekend for holiday bazaars. First one is happening today and tomorrow at the White Center Library (1409 SW 107th), where the WC Library Guild ‘s Holiday Bazaar and Book Sale has a variety of treasures and, well, knickknacks: Houseplants too, and even a freebie here and there: The most unusual items we spotted: Three small collections of old Northwest candidate buttons, including one for the legendary Senator Henry “Scoop” Jackson . Shop the bazaar until 4 pm today and again 11 am-4 pm tomorrow. Money raised goes to library programs.

posts.title: Got batteries to recycle? Greenbridge event this Saturday
posts.description: (Also published on partner site West Seattle Blog ) You can’t throw them out. You can’t put them in regular weekly curbside recycling. But you CAN recycle batteries at a free dropoff event in Greenbridge this Saturday, 10 am-2 pm – here’s the announcement we just received: With holiday preparations and gift-giving in motion, the question is what to do with used batteries in the old holiday decorations, toys, smart phones and laptops that will be replaced in this season of giving. The answer: Bring your used batteries to a battery collection event organized by WM and King County, in collaboration with the National Waste & Recycling Association (NWRA) and The Battery Network . The collection event is free and will feature Woodsy Owl®, America’s iconic conservation mascot: Saturday, Nov. 21, from 10 am – 2 pm, at Wiley Center, 9800 8th Ave. SW, Seattle Residents can safely and responsibly recycle household batteries at this event, including button cell, AAAA through D and rechargeable lit
